blocks.text: COX’S BAZAR, Bangladesh — Hundreds of Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh sat in front of a big screen at their sprawling camp in Cox’s Bazar, watching the news from the Netherlands, where the U.N.’s top court ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation. For many, the historic verdict on Thursday represented a “small victory” — offering a glimmer of hope that someday they would be able to return safely to their homes in Myanmar, across the border from Bangladesh.
